tldr: COPRA is an in-context learning agent that uses a general-purpose LLM (GPT-4) within a stateful backtracking search to generate formal proofs in Lean and Coq, outperforming few-shot prompting and competing with finetuned approaches like REPROVER.
contributions: A new approach called COPRA combining in-context learning with search, knowledge retrieval, and rich feedback from the proof environment
A systematic study comparing GPT-4-based COPRA against few-shot GPT-4, GPT-3.5 ablations, and state-of-the-art finetuned baselines
An open-source implementation supporting both Lean and Coq proof environments
methods: COPRA performs a GPT-4-directed depth-first search over tactic sequences in formal proof environments. At each step, it retrieves relevant lemmas/definitions from an external database, serializes the current proof state stack, failure history, and optional informal proof context into a prompt, and queries GPT-4 to propose the next tactic. Executed tactics are fed back into the search: successful progress continues the search, while errors or non-progress states are recorded in a failure dictionary and the search backtracks. A symbolic progress check based on a partial order over proof states prevents cyclic tactic sequences.
results: On miniF2F-test (244 Lean theorems), COPRA achieved pass@1 of 26.63% without retrieval, 29.09% with retrieval, and 29.92% with retrieval plus informal proofs, outperforming REPROVER (25.00%), LLEMMA-34b (25.82%), and LLEMMA-7b (26.23%). COPRA solved more than twice as many problems as few-shot GPT-4 (13.52%). On the CompCert Coq benchmark (118 theorems), COPRA also outperformed few-shot baselines. COPRA found correct proofs using approximately 16x fewer queries than REPROVER and proved them almost 3x faster. GPT-3.5 and CodeLlama instantiations were significantly weaker (9.02% and 5.73% respectively).
limitations: Evaluation on CompCert used only 118 of 501 theorems due to budgetary constraints
COPRA with weaker models (GPT-3.5, CodeLlama) performed substantially worse, indicating GPT-4-scale models are critical
The approach relies on a black-box LLM, making it dependent on the capabilities of underlying model quality
Cost and latency are concerns due to repeated GPT-4 queries, though the method uses far fewer queries than finetuned baselines
